title: Classify a tick with Jev, and never classify a role tick
description:
The call itself, which is already proven: 49 ticks classified on 2026-09-22 in three requests for $0.0022. The measurement note on the parent has the working shape, and two details cost real time to find:

  - The response nests ONE DEEPER than the model page shows: result -> {state, result: {model, answers, usage}}. Reading result.answers gets zero answers and no error.
  - Questions are 'evaluated in parallel and in isolation against the same state', so an epic's ticks batch into ONE call with one Choice question per tick keyed by tick id. That is what makes it three calls rather than 49, and the isolation is what makes it safe rather than merely cheap.

The precondition, which is not an optimisation: A TICK CARRYING A ROLE IS NEVER CLASSIFIED. [roles.*] already maps review and closeout to a model. The measurement put three role ticks through the classifier and got mechanical 0.32, diagnosis 0.61 and design 0.99 for the same kind of work, because the enum has no right answer for 'read a diff and judge it' and Jev must pick one of five wrong ones. Skip them.

Input is the tick's title, description and acceptance criteria. Criteria objects with what/not_for/examples per work type are what produced the measured distribution - carry them over rather than paraphrasing, since they are the thing that was measured.

Return the FULL probability distribution, not just the argmax: the next tick routes on mass and cannot recover what an argmax threw away.
acceptance_criteria: A role-less tick is classified into the enum with its full probability distribution, a role-carrying tick is never sent to the classifier, an epic's ticks batch into one call, and a classifier that is unreachable returns a distinguishable no-answer rather than an error that stops a run
